records.document_summary: Teodor Burada's published school roll for the Romanian school in Ghiorgea lists Nicola Cican among pupils in the 1888–1889 school year.
records.status: Documented historical occurrence; identity linkage to later Nicolae Cican unresolved
records.notes: Potentially important for Nicolae Cican's pre-America life, but the source gives no age, parentage or other identifier sufficient for a definitive merge. Important source correction: Burada's heading places the 73-pupil roll under the Pleasa school; the text explains that winter classes moved to Ghiorgea/Corcea and local Romanian children also attended. A separate permanent Ghiorgea school is mentioned as functioning since 1883. Therefore this occurrence is not labeled as a standalone Ghiorgea-school enrolment. Source wording control: Burada's surrounding discussion explains the relationship between the Pleasa and Ghiorgea schools, but the actual 1888–1889 name list is introduced as the pupils of the Ghiorgea school. The archive therefore records Ghiorgea as the place of the school roll while preserving the broader Pleasa winter-school context.

records.document_summary: Haralambie Balamaci's scholarly biography states that Nicolae (Culicea) Cican emigrated to America in 1901 after graduating that year from the Romanian high school in Bitola.
records.notes: This establishes a dated graduation/emigration claim for the later Nicolae Cican, but does not yet prove that he is the Nicola Cican listed in the 1888–1889 Ghiorgea school roll.

records.document_summary: Balamaci's study states that Nicolae Cican, then president/secretary of Society Farsarotul, returned to Bitola for the Ottoman Romanians' Congress held 10–11 July 1909 and then returned to America.
records.notes: This is an important geographical continuity point: the later Nicolae Cican demonstrably returned to Bitola in 1909. It does not establish the identity of the 1888 schoolboy.

records.document_summary: Balamaci states that Nicolae Cican returned to Corcea in 1913, where he worked as a banker and emigration agent.
records.notes: Provides a dated return-to-Corcea anchor before the 1914 violence documented by contemporary press.
